YOUR ITEMS (ranked VS screen + countdown, found phone-vs-phone on build apk6; bug texts in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop2-bugs.json, taskIds pregame-found-countdown-reduced and avatars-idle-still; full phone evidence in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop-1.json fixcheck checks 'K2 B37-still' and 'K3 B43-badges-phone3'):
1) K2: in the FIRST ranked game after app launch, GO! stays fully visible 1.75 s before the board appears (later games 1.0-1.1 s; expected per motion.md ~0.4-0.6 s). Likely the match/board screen's first mount (route chunk, Board/Keypad/fonts/avatars/sounds) is heavy the first time and GO! waits for it. Find what is cold on the first game (compare with what the round-loop1 warm-up in apps/mobile/src/screens/home/warmModes.ts already preloads) and warm it earlier (during search/VS) or make the reveal not wait on it.
2) K3/B43: (a) in 1 of 5 games (reduced motion ON) phone 3's tile stayed 'מתחבר…' with '1/2 מוכנים · מחכים שכולם יתחברו…' on BOTH phones through the whole VS and the count started anyway — find how the ready state of each player reaches the VS tiles (client + protocol + server room state) and why one player's ready can be missed/never re-sent (race between join and VS mount? reduced-motion path?). The count must not start with a badge still 'מתחבר…', or the badge must reflect the real state. (b) the 'מוכן' badges appear in a single frame and the whole VS block jumps up ~50 device px then settles ~13 px back: badges must not change layout (reserve their space) and should fade/pop per motion.md (respect Reduced Motion). (c) the avatar 'nod' on ready shows only 2 frames of change, not the ~0.9 s nod — check it runs on the UI thread and isn't cut by the cross-fade.

items.id: K2 pregame-found-countdown-reduced (GO! 1.75 s in the first ranked game)
items.rootCause: The slow part was the sound players, not the board. sfx creates each sound's expo-audio player the first time the sound is used, and keeps it. expo-audio builds each player on the UI thread while the JS thread waits (runBlocking, the same cost found in T3-FIRST-PLAY-SLOW), so no frame is drawn until it exists. When the game screen mounts it calls preloadCues(GAME_CUES): 11 sounds, 13 players. In the first game of a run, all 13 were built in a row right under GO!. On top of that, 'go' built its own player when GO! was first drawn, 'countdownBeat' did the same at '3', and 'matchFound' at the VS. From the second game on, all of these players already exist, which explains 1.75 s in the first game against 1.0–1.1 s later. The round-loop1 warm-up (warmModes) only creates ui_tap. The game screen's code (screens/game, which the lazily loaded /game route needs) was also cold. Skia is not part of this: AmbientCanvas already loads it on Home.
items.fix: New file apps/mobile/src/screens/match/warmGame.ts. MatchScreen runs warmGameLater() while the model is 'search' (connecting or searching). It starts 400 ms after the search screen is up, then runs one step per idle moment (whenIdle), so each stall is short and there is never one long stall. Order: the matchFound, countdownBeat and go players first, then require('../game') (the game screen's code), then the GAME_CUES players one at a time. It stops when the search ends ('found'), so nothing is built while the VS, the count or GO! is drawn. Anything left over is built by GameScreen as before. With sound off it creates no players. Docs: a new section in docs/PERF.md ('המשחק המדורג הראשון: GO! ארוך').
items.test:
New apps/mobile/src/screens/match/__tests__/warmGame.test.tsx, using the real sfx and feedback with expo-audio from nativeMocks:
(1) Before 400 ms nothing is created. After the search, all 16 players of the flow and game sounds exist and the game code is loaded. Then found, ready, countdown, GO and the board: the cues, plus GameScreen's preloadCues(), create no new player. This fails on the old code (0 players created during the search).
(2) With a manual idle queue: exactly one step per idle callback, and nothing more after stop().

items.deviceCheck: Needs a new APK. Sound on (the default), reduced motion off, both phones. Force-stop the app, launch it, Settings, back to Home. Then 'שחק' → '2 שחקנים' → 'מהיר' → 'מצא יריב' on both phones at the same moment (the first ranked game of the process). Record at 50 ms frames. Expected: GO! fully visible about 1.0–1.1 s before the board, the same as in the next games (was 1.75 s). The search screen's radar may show a few short hitches in its first ~1–2 s (the players being built). Also check that the matchFound chime, the 3·2·1 beats and the GO sound still play. A second game should be unchanged (1.0–1.1 s).

items.id: K3a B43 (1 of 5): phone 3 stayed 'מתחבר…' / '1/2' through the whole VS and the count started anyway
items.rootCause: Ready state path: the game room's join hook on the server (matchmaking/service.ts claim().join) adds the player to match.ready and calls sendReady. sendReady sends the full list to every member over matchmaking. MatchmakingClient 'ready' replaces match.ready, and seatsOf turns that into seat.ready on the VS. When the last player joins at or after found+1200 ms (FOUND_HOLD), everyoneIn starts the countdown in the same server tick. So the 'ready' with both players and 'countdown' arrive together. React batches them, and the screen goes straight from 'found' to 'countdown'. Or the game room's own startsAt arrives first, on the other WebSocket (MatchmakingClient.onHost puts the phase into 'countdown' before matchmaking's 'ready' arrives). MatchScreen keeps the VS under the count with the last 'found' model it rendered, so that model never saw the last ready. Both phones therefore faded the VS out on 'מתחבר…' and '1/2' while the count, correctly, started. Phone 3 joined late, a network or busy-JS issue during its VS. The badge showed the true state until the very end; the bug is that the VS under the count was never updated. Reduced motion is not the cause: it only shows the badges from the start.
items.fix: MatchScreen.tsx: once the count runs, the VS kept under it gets allReady(model): every seat ready, readyCount = total, allReady true. The countdown's own seats already work this way, because the server counts only when everyone is in. It is memoized (useMemo), so the memoized VS re-renders at most once, frozen: the badge changes and no avatar starts moving under the count. Docs: motion.md vs.slam row, 01-SPEC §10.
items.test: MatchScreen.test.tsx, it.each: 'the last "ready" with the count, in the same batch' and 'after the game room's count, on the other connection: the VS under the count says everyone is ready, never "מתחבר…" (QA K3, B43 1 of 5)'. Setup: reduced motion on, ready ['me'], then 1.1 s of VS showing opp 'מתחבר…' and 1/2. Then ready and countdown in one act, or the host's startsAt first. Expected: '3' shows, seat-opp-ready 'מוכן', 2/2 and 'כל השחקנים מוכנים', with no seat-opp-connecting. Both cases fail on the old code (checked by turning off allReady).
items.deviceCheck: Hard to force on demand, since one player has to join the game room late. Phones 1 and 3, reduced motion on, then off; 5+ ranked 2p 'מהיר' games started at the same moment, recorded at 50 ms frames. Expected in every game: no frame where '3' or the cross-fade into it shows a tile with 'מתחבר…' or '1/2 מוכנים · מחכים שכולם יתחברו…'. A phone that really connects late may still show 'מתחבר…' during the VS (that is the real state), but the VS fades out on 'מוכן' / '2/2 כל השחקנים מוכנים'.

items.id: K3b B43: badges appear in one frame and the VS block jumps ~50 px then settles ~13 px
items.rootCause: SeatTile rendered the badge only when showReady was true (badge 22 dp + the tile's gap). When the badges popped at found+800, both tiles grew. The VS column is vertically centred in the ScrollView (justifyContent center), so the whole block moved up by about half the growth, and settled again as the frames caught up. The badge also had no enter animation, although motion.md says the badges 'pop' (the pop spring, used for chips and badges).
items.fix: parts.tsx SeatTile: until the badges show, an empty slot of metrics.badgeHeight keeps their place (testID seat-<id>-badge-slot), so the tile's layout never changes. The badge is wrapped in BadgePop: a pop spring from 0.6 to 1 (metrics.vs.badgePopFrom) while fading in (stateChange 240 ms). Transforms only, so nothing around it moves. It is keyed by state, so a connecting badge that turns ready pops again. Reduced motion, or the VS kept frozen under the count: shown at once, nothing animates. Docs: motion.md vs.slam row (and its reduced-motion column), 01-SPEC §10.
items.test: MatchScreen.test.tsx: 'the "מוכן" badges move nothing as they pop: their place is kept from the start, and they pop in (QA K3)'. Checks a badgeHeight slot in both tiles before the pop, a badge of the same height after it, and the pop going from {opacity 0, scale 0.6} to {1, 1}. Also 'reduced motion: the badges are there with the VS, whole, nothing popping'. The first test fails on the old code (no slot).
items.deviceCheck: Reduced motion off, ranked 2p, recorded at 50 ms frames. When the 'מוכן' badges appear (~0.8 s after 'נמצא יריב!'), the header chip, title, tiles, VS badge and status line must not move by even 1 px (was ~50 px up, then ~13 px back). Each badge should scale up from small and fade in over ~0.25–0.45 s rather than appear in one frame. Reduced motion on: the badges are there with the VS and nothing moves.

items.id: K3c: the 'ready' nod showed only 2 frames of change instead of ~0.9 s
items.rootCause: The nod is a Reanimated plan on the UI thread (AvatarArt), and the count's cross-fade does not stop it: the frozen VS lets a running motion finish. What stopped it was the count's preparation. FoundView reported onSettled 2 frames after the badges were drawn, and MatchScreen then mounted the whole countdown view hidden behind the VS: two avatars, the 81-cell ghost board and the header. Its JS (~300 ms on an A16) and then its first draw on the UI thread, where every new SVG shape re-applies the props of recently moved views (docs/PERF.md B14/B32, including the nodding layers), held the UI thread from about 0.3 s after the pop. That matches QA's changes at 0.15 and 0.3 s and none after. There is also a design limit: badges at found+800 plus a 900 ms nod is longer than the count at found+1200 (+240 ms fade), so at most ~0.4–0.65 s of the nod can ever be seen.
items.fix: FoundView.tsx: onSettled now fires once the VS itself is drawn (afterFrames(SWAP_FRAMES) after its first render, in both motion modes), not after the badges. The count is then built behind the VS before the badges pop, and the nod runs on a free UI thread. The rest of the M1 design is unchanged (cross-fade, frozen VS, count anchored to its first drawn frame). Docs: motion.md countdown.digit row, 01-SPEC §10.
items.test: MatchScreen.test.tsx: 'the count gets ready unseen behind the VS once the VS is drawn, before the badges pop' (the hidden countdown exists at found+100 ms, before any seat-*-ready). The FoundView test 'QA B43' now also expects onSettled to have fired before the badges, at +299 ms. Both fail on the old code (checked by restoring the badges && active condition).
items.deviceCheck: Reduced motion off, ranked 2p, recorded at 50 ms frames. From the frame where the 'מוכן' badges appear until the cross-fade into '3', the avatar areas should change in every frame, a continuous nod of about 0.4–0.6 s (it starts at found+0.8 s and the VS fades at ~found+1.2 s). Before, there were only 2 changed frames. The smile should stay. If the full 0.9 s nod has to be visible, that needs Moshe's decision on badgesAtMs or FOUND_HOLD; see notes.

rep.notes: Client-only changes: no server change and no deploy needed. No new UI strings, so no i18n keys changed. Ran 'npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit' (clean), eslint on all changed files (clean), and prettier --write on the changed code and test files. Tests run, all passing: the 6 match suites (incl. MatchScreen, matchFaces, rankedResults, MatchErrors), the new warmGame test, composedText, startupGraph, ranked.e2e, warmPressCue, the services tests and the doc-reading tests (transitions, sfx, friendsDocs, levelsSpecDocs, localizationDocs, noLayoutAnimationsInGame, mapMotion). In tests that mock services/feedback with only cue(), building the warm-up's steps throws, so the warm-up does nothing there and does not load the game screen in those suites. K3c design limit for Moshe: badges at found+800 plus a 900 ms nod is longer than the server's count at found+1200 (+240 ms cross-fade), so even after this fix only about 0.4–0.65 s of the nod can be seen. Seeing the whole nod would need badgesAtMs at about 300 or a longer FOUND_HOLD_MS. That changes the timings in motion.md and on the server, so I did not change it. The late join behind K3a (phone 3 joining the game room ≥1.2 s after 'found') is real network or JS latency. The server behaves correctly: it counts only once everyone is in. The FlowFallback act() console warning in the match tests is unrelated to these changes and was left as is. reps.brief: YOUR ITEM (ranked game surrender dialog; bug text in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop2-bugs.json, taskId postgame-results-v2-new-game-ranked): tapping 'כן, להיכנע' (testID ranked-surrender-confirm) about 1.0-1.5 s after tapping 'כניעה' closes the dialog WITHOUT surrendering, 2 of 9 times; waiting 2 s always worked. Find the dialog/sheet component and its enter animation + scrim/backdrop press handling (and whether the confirm button is disabled/not-yet-interactive during enter, or a re-render/state reset swallows the press, or the server surrender message is sent before something is ready). The confirm press must always surrender. Check other confirm dialogs using the same component for the same flaw.

items.rootCause: Client side, in the shared ConfirmModal (apps/mobile/src/components/ui/ConfirmModal.tsx), which the ranked surrender dialog (RankedSurrender) uses. The panel slides up through usePresence (translateY (1-progress)*panelHeight; 320 ms nominal). The full-screen Scrim behind it called onCancel on any tap from the first frame. On the A16 the JS thread is busy in a live ranked game, so the Modal window can show, and the enter animation can start, well after the 'כניעה' tap. Until the panel arrives, the place where 'כן, להיכנע' ends up (258,1970) is scrim. An early tap at that spot hit the scrim, and onCancel ran closeConfirm: the dialog closed, nothing was sent, and the game went on. That fits the symptom exactly: the dialog closed with no surrender, and waiting 2 s always worked. Other causes ruled out: (1) Nothing else sets confirmOpen to false; only closeConfirm (cancel, scrim, back, escape) and confirmEnd do. (2) The confirm Button has no disabled or loading gate, since RankedSurrender never passes `confirming`. A re-render with a new onConfirm does not remount the Pressable. (3) The server would not drop it: the engine accepts 'surrender' in any status except waiting or over, including every freeze, and the gate limit of 2 per second is not reached by one send.
items.fix: ConfirmModal: the scrim's onPress now goes through scrimPress, which calls onCancel only when progress.get() >= 1, meaning the dialog has finished entering. On the JS thread this is a synchronous read of the UI value in Reanimated 4.5. Until then a scrim tap does nothing and the dialog stays open. The confirm and cancel buttons, Android back (onRequestClose) and the escape gesture still work from the first frame. This applies with reduced motion too (the 200 ms fade) and to both placements. The onCancel doc comment was updated. Because every confirm dialog uses ConfirmModal, they all get the fix: the ranked surrender, the friends and practice end dialog, the level exit ('לצאת מהשלב?'), moderation block, account settings, terms, language pickers, invite link, ChooseName, and the Puzzle and Tap level dialogs. No new strings, so i18n is unchanged.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/components/ui/__tests__/ConfirmModal.test.tsx gets a new it.each over bottom/center × reduce motion off/on. Two scrim taps during the enter (one at 0 ms, one at 100 ms) do not call onCancel, and the dialog stays. 'כן, להיכנע' pressed during the enter calls onConfirm at once. After the full sheetIn, a scrim tap cancels once. On the old code (scrim → onCancel) all 4 cases fail; with the fix all pass. The existing 'everything else cancels' test now advances by sheetIn before the scrim tap. Passing: ConfirmModal + RankedSurrender (33), and connection/*, moderation/*, ranked.e2e (278 in total). tsc -p apps/mobile is clean, eslint is clean, prettier reports no changes.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 3 (SM-A165F), ranked 2-player fast game against phone 1, new APK. (1) Tap 'כניעה' (785,499), then tap at once (about 0.3 s, no uiautomator dump in between) at the final position of 'כן, להיכנע' (258,1970). Expected: the dialog does NOT close without a surrender. Either the tap hit the button and Results open (surrender), or it landed while the panel was still rising and nothing happened, with the dialog still open. In the second case a second tap on 'כן, להיכנע' must surrender. Repeat about 10 times at delays of 0.3, 0.6, 1.0 and 1.5 s. 'Dialog closed and the game goes on' must never happen. (2) Scrim still cancels: tap 'כניעה', wait 2 s, tap the dark area above the sheet (e.g. 540,300). The dialog closes and the game goes on. (3) The same with reduced motion on (the fade). (4) Spot check on another ConfirmModal: in a stage, tap X, then quickly tap the dark area. It stays open; after about 1 s the dark area closes it.

rep.notes: Client-side fix only, so deployNeeded = false. Only ConfirmModal's scrim changed. The shared Scrim component, Sheet and ArsenalOverlay were not touched. Sheet (report sheet, menus, avatar picker) and the arsenal have the same shape, a scrim that closes from the first frame, but there an early tap only closes a menu and loses no confirmed action. If you want the same rule there, it is the same one-line guard in Sheet.tsx's Scrim onPress, plus an adjustment to the Sheet, AvatarPicker and ArsenalOverlay tests that tap the scrim right after render. A side finding: GameScreen does not show anything for a server 'rejected' on surrender (it does not listen to 'rejected' for surrender). The engine accepts surrender in every status except waiting/over, so this is not the cause here, but a refused surrender would also fail silently. No adb, APK or deploy was done, and no git commands that change state were run.

reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (staged practice levels, found on build apk7; bug texts in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop2-bugs.json, taskIds levels-exit, levels-freeze-background, levels-freeze-ready; QA task text: node docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/task.cjs <taskId>):
1) levels-exit (most important): Android system Back while 'מוכן?' (ready) or the boss intro ('שלב בוס!') is showing returns to the map immediately with no 'לצאת מהשלב?' dialog, and the level keeps running hidden: pressing 'שחק' on the same level ~22 s later shows the running stage with 'התשובה: D1' and then a result. Back must behave as the spec says for these phases (exit dialog, or a clean cancel that disposes the level host/timers — read docs/01-SPEC.md staged practice + the levels docs to decide), and a level session must never survive leaving the screen.
2) levels-freeze-background: the recents thumbnail shows the full board while the stage is frozen (the 'המשחק עצור' cover is drawn too late). Make the cover appear before Android takes the snapshot (e.g. react to AppState 'blur'/'inactive' as well as 'background' on Android, or another cheap approach) — keep it small; FLAG_SECURE is NOT acceptable (blocks screenshots).
3) levels-freeze-ready: about 0.5-0.6 s after 'מוכן?' ends the board first draws at full width (x 45-1034 of 1080) with a full-width keypad, then jumps to x 96-984 centred and the board top moves ~50 px. The first render must use the final size (measure the available room before showing the board, or keep it hidden until measured).

items.rootCause: app/levels/play.tsx registered no Android back handler for the run's phases before the stage screen exists: 'איך משחקים', 'מוכן?' and the boss intro (all ReadyView), plus the short blank while the session starts. Only TapLevelScreen, useStageShell and GameScreen register one, and only in the 'playing' phase. So back fell through to the navigator's default goBack, with no question. On the phone that pop left the run mounted and running, so its ReadyView timer started the stage behind the map. I could not reproduce the survival itself in Jest: there the pop does unmount the screen. The fix therefore does not rely on that pop.
items.fix: StageRun in app/levels/play.tsx now registers its own BackHandler when it mounts. Stage screens mount later, so they register later and are heard first. Before a stage screen takes back (tutorial, ready or boss intro, or the stage still starting), back is a clean cancel with no dialog. The phase becomes a new 'left' state that renders an empty view, so no ReadyView timer runs and no LevelStage or session is ever created. Then onMap() leaves through the same router.dismissTo('/levels') path that 'למפה' uses, along with its leave watchdog. Nothing is stored, and the stage does not count as played. In the result phase back still goes to the navigator, as before. Spec reasoning: §19.8 says the stage and its clock start only after 'מוכן?'. The 'לצאת מהשלב?' dialog ('0 stars, the next stage opens') belongs to a running stage (§6.6 and components §19.6), so before the start, back cancels.
items.test: New file apps/mobile/src/screens/levels/__tests__/levelPlayBack.test.tsx, 5 tests: back during 'מוכן?' and during a boss intro gives the map and the stage never mounts, even 60 s later; from the map, back during 'מוכן?' and then 'שחק' again starts fresh from 'מוכן?'; back during 'איך משחקים' also cancels; once the stage screen is up, its own back is heard first. With the handler disabled, 3 of the 5 tests fail.
items.deviceCheck: Phone, Hebrew. 1) Levels map, choose L001, press 'שחק'. While 'מוכן?' shows (about 1 s), press Android Back: you go straight to the map, with no dialog. 2) Wait about 25 s, then press 'שחק' again on L001: a new 'מוכן?' appears, the stage starts from its full time, and there is no 'התשובה: D1' and no ready-made result. 3) Do the same on a boss (L010 or L020) during 'שלב בוס!': map, then 25 s later 'שחק' gives a new boss intro. The map does not change after the back (no stars, and the next stage does not open because of it). 4) Mid-stage, Back still opens 'לצאת מהשלב?' ('המשך לשחק' and 'יציאה' work as before). 5) If 'איך משחקים' appears (a new kind), Back on it also goes to the map.

items.rootCause: The D65 freeze (BackgroundPause, used by levelSession) listened only to AppState 'change'. On Android that fires 'background' at onPause, after the system has already taken the task picture for Recents. The cover ('המשחק עצור') was drawn only after the JS round-trip, so the Recents card showed the full board. The window's 'blur' arrives earlier, when the app loses focus.
items.fix: levelSession now also listens to AppState 'blur' and 'focus', through a new optional dep windowFocus (by default AppState on Android, null on iOS, where 'inactive' already arrives in time). 'blur' calls the existing freeze.background(), so it is a real freeze with the cover, not just a picture. 'focus' when currentState is 'active' gives the same 3, 2, 1 countdown. The listeners are removed in close(). An RN Modal (Dialog) also takes window focus on Android, so a new module src/components/ui/modalWindows.ts counts the app's own open windows: ConfirmModal and Sheet each call useModalWindow(mounted), one added line plus one import each. A 'blur' while one of them is open is ignored, so the stage keeps running under 'לצאת מהשלב?' as before. FLAG_SECURE was not used.
items.test: levelSession.test.ts, new describe '[D65] Android: the freeze comes with the window's blur', 5 tests: Recents (the cover is up at blur, before background; focus before active does nothing; active gives 3,2,1 with the same time left); notification shade (blur then focus gives 3,2,1); the app's own dialog does not freeze; backgroundPause off does not listen and close() removes the listeners; by default the listeners are registered on Android and not on iOS. New file src/components/ui/__tests__/modalWindows.test.tsx: ConfirmModal and Sheet are counted while open and stop being counted once they have left.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 1, Hebrew. 1) Start stage 34 (puzzle) or 35. In the middle, press Recents: the app's card in Recents shows the cover ('המשחק עצור'), not the board. 2) Return to the app: the cover shows 3, 2, 1 and the stage continues with the same time. 3) Press Home and return: during the opening animation the board is no longer seen under the cover. 4) Pull down the notification shade mid-stage: the stage freezes (cover). Push the shade back up: 3, 2, 1 and the stage continues. 5) Regression: press X mid-stage and the 'לצאת מהשלב?' dialog opens with the board visible behind it, no cover, and the clock keeps running. 'המשך לשחק' returns with no 3,2,1.

items.rootCause: GameScreen (and also TapLevelScreen and PuzzleLevelScreen) took the board room's height only from onLayout. In the first render roomHeight was null, so boardSide fell back to min(width - gutters, 358 dp) and the board and keypad drew at full width. Only when onLayout arrived (async, about 0.5 s on the A16) did they shrink to the room's height and move.
items.fix: New hook src/screens/game/useRoomHeight.ts. It gives the room View a callback ref that reads its laid-out height at the commit, through a new geometry.layoutHeightOf(node), which uses the RN element API getBoundingClientRect. In the New Architecture the tree is laid out before refs and layout effects run, and an update made then is drawn in the same frame, so the first frame already has the final size. onLayout keeps updating the height as before, and is the only source where the API is missing (tests). The hook is wired into GameScreen (the duel and fill stages, and practice and ranked too), TapLevelScreen and PuzzleLevelScreen. It changes only the source of roomHeight.
items.test: New file apps/mobile/src/screens/levels/__tests__/stageFirstFrame.test.tsx: with layoutHeightOf giving 300, a fill-box stage (GameScreen) and a find stage (TapLevelScreen) draw cell A1 at boardGeometry(300) with no onLayout at all; the old code draws 358, so this fails on it. Also: without the API the behaviour is unchanged (358 until onLayout), plus unit tests for layoutHeightOf. All the existing GameScreen tests, which fire layout on board-room, pass.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 1, Hebrew. Levels, stage 35 (duel to 30), 'שחק'. Take frames or a recording of the moment 'מוכן?' ends. The first frame of the board must already be centred at its final size (about x 96–984 of 1080 on the A16), with the keypad at the same width. There must be no full-width frame (x 45–1034) and no jump of about 50 px in the board's top. Repeat on a find stage, a puzzle stage (34), and one practice game (the board's entry animation is unchanged).

items.id: K3a B43 (1 of 5): phone 3 stayed 'מתחבר…' / '1/2' through the whole VS and the count started anyway
items.rootCause:
This is how the ready state reaches the VS. On the server, the game room's join hook (matchmaking/service.ts, claim().join) adds the player to match.ready and calls sendReady, which sends the full list to every member over the matchmaking connection. MatchmakingClient 'ready' replaces match.ready, and seatsOf turns it into seat.ready on the VS.
When the last player joins at or after found+1200 ms (FOUND_HOLD), everyoneIn starts the countdown in the same server tick. The 'ready' with both players and the 'countdown' then arrive together, React batches them, and the screen goes straight from 'found' to 'countdown'. Or the game room's own startsAt arrives first, on the other WebSocket: MatchmakingClient.onHost moves the phase to 'countdown' before the matchmaking 'ready' arrives.
MatchScreen kept the VS under the count with the last 'found' model it had rendered, and that model never saw the last ready. So both phones faded the VS out on 'מתחבר…' and '1/2' while the count started, correctly. Phone 3 joined late (network, or busy JS). Reduced motion is not the cause.
items.fix: MatchScreen.tsx (from the first round, unchanged): once the count runs, the VS kept under it gets allReady(model): every seat ready, readyCount = total. The countdown's own seats already work this way, because the server counts only when everyone is in. It is memoized, so the frozen VS re-renders at most once. Review note (low), addressed in docs: motion.md now states this one exception to 'nothing new is drawn under the count'. Badges, the status line and '2/2' change once, frozen, with nothing moving.
items.test: MatchScreen.test.tsx, it.each, two cases: 'the last "ready" with the count, in the same batch', and 'after the game room's count, on the other connection'. In both, the VS under the count shows 'מוכן', 2/2 and 'כל השחקנים מוכנים', never seat-opp-connecting. Both fail on the old code.

Expected in every game: no frame where '3', or the cross-fade into it, shows a tile with 'מתחבר…' or '1/2 מוכנים · מחכים שכולם יתחברו…'. A phone that really connects late may show 'מתחבר…' during the VS, because that is the real state, but the VS fades out on 'מוכן' and '2/2 כל השחקנים מוכנים'.

items.id: K3c: the 'ready' nod showed only 2 frames of change instead of ~0.9 s
items.rootCause:
The nod is a Reanimated plan on the UI thread (AvatarArt), and the cross-fade does not stop it. What stopped it was the count's preparation. FoundView reported onSettled after the badges, and MatchScreen then mounted the whole countdown view hidden behind the VS (two avatars, the 81-cell ghost board, the header). Its JS (~300 ms on an A16) and then its first UI-thread draw held the UI thread through the nod.
Review point (medium), accepted: the first-round fix fired onSettled 2 frames after the VS was drawn. That moved the stall into the VS slam (a slam spring of about 400–530 ms) rather than removing it. On a fast phone the count's draw would land in the slam's strongest swing.
Design limit: badges at found+800 plus a 900 ms nod is longer than the count at found+1200 (+240 ms fade), so at most ~0.4–0.65 s of the nod can ever be seen.
items.fix:
FoundView.tsx: onSettled (which prepares the count behind the VS) now fires after the VS is drawn (afterFrames) plus min(metrics.vs.settleMs = 250, (badgesAt − metrics.vs.prepareLeadMs = 400) − now), never below 0. In other words: once the slam has swung (the slam spring is within ~6% of its end by 250 ms), and at the latest 400 ms before the badges, which is the count's React work plus its first draw. A VS drawn late, past that deadline, prepares at once. Reduced motion (nothing slams, no nod) prepares as soon as the VS is drawn.
On QA's A16 numbers (VS first frame ~found+200): the prepare starts at +400, the JS runs until ~+700 on the JS thread (the slam keeps running on the UI thread), and the draw falls at ~+700–800, between the slam's end and the badges at +800. On a fast phone: +300, drawn by ~+450. The values are tunable in metrics.ts. Docs: motion.md countdown.digit row, 01-SPEC §10, the MatchScreen header comment.

- New: 'reduced motion: nothing slams, so the count gets ready behind the VS as soon as the VS is drawn' (exists at +100).
- FoundView 'QA B43' (VS drawn 500 ms late) still expects onSettled before the badges, at once.

(b) The nod: from the frame where the 'מוכן' badges appear until the cross-fade into '3', the avatar areas should change in every frame, a continuous nod of about 0.4–0.6 s (before: only 2 changed frames). The smile stays.

items.rootCause: Two client-side paths can close the ranked surrender dialog without a surrender. I can't tell from the QA data which one happened at 20:37:56 and 21:01:47. (A) The scrim. ConfirmModal's full-screen Scrim called onCancel on any tap from the first frame. While the panel is still sliding up (usePresence, 320 ms nominal, later on a busy A16 JS thread), the spot where 'כן, להיכנע' ends up (258,1970) is scrim, so an early tap cancelled. (B) A connection blip. I was wrong earlier when I said only closeConfirm and confirmEnd set confirmOpen to false. GameScreen also closes the dialog while rendering: when `blocked` turns true (an opponent freeze, self-reconnecting, connecting, error, opponentLeft; GameScreen.tsx, the wasBlocked block), when `selfOffline` (the D42 soft phase) turns true (the wasOffline block), and in showResults' closeWindows. All of these closed it silently, with no breadcrumb and no toast. A blip shorter than a frame or two leaves no visible connection screen, so to the tester it looks exactly like a lost tap. The reviewer is right. (C) A third silent path. If the surrender is refused (the RemoteGameHost refuses it locally as 'disconnected' when the link is not live at the moment of the press, or the server sends 'rejected'), the 'refused' effect is handled only for interferences. The dialog is already gone and the game goes on, with nothing said. The server itself accepts 'surrender' in every status except waiting/over, so it is not the source of (C) in a running game.
items.fix: 1) Unchanged from the first round: ConfirmModal's scrim cancels only once the enter animation has finished (scrimPress: progress.get() >= 1). The buttons, Android back and escape work from the first frame. items.rootCause: app/levels/play.tsx registered no Android back handler for the phases that come before the stage screen exists: 'איך משחקים', 'מוכן?' and the boss intro (all ReadyView), plus the short blank while the session starts. Only TapLevelScreen, useStageShell and GameScreen register one, and only in the 'playing' phase. So back fell through to the navigator's default goBack, with no question. On the phone that pop left the run mounted and running, so its ReadyView timer started the stage behind the map. I could not reproduce in Jest why the route survived; there the pop unmounts the screen. The fix therefore does not rely on the navigator's pop in any phase.
items.fix: StageRun registers its own BackHandler when it mounts. Stage screens mount later, so their handlers are heard first. (1) Before a stage screen takes back (tutorial, ready or boss intro, or the stage still starting), back is a clean cancel with no dialog. The phase becomes 'left', which renders an empty view, so no ReadyView timer runs and no LevelStage or session is ever created. The exit then goes through onMap(), which uses router.dismissTo('/levels'), the same path as 'למפה', with its leave watchdog. (2) Review fix: back in the result phase now also goes through onMap(), called once, the same as 'למפה'. Before, it returned false and fell to the navigator's default pop. Now no exit from levels/play depends on that pop. While leaving, back stays taken, so there is no second pop under the one already leaving. If dismissTo stalls, the existing watchdog shows FlowFallback after resultsWatchdogMs. The spec now has one line in §6.6 (levels bullet), marked as awaiting Moshe's approval: back before the start cancels with no dialog and counts nothing; back on the result is 'למפה'.

items.rootCause: Android takes the task picture for Recents as the app leaves: after the window's 'blur' and before onPause/'background'. The D65 cover ('המשחק עצור') is React state, so it is drawn only after a JS round-trip. With only 'background' (the original code), and even with 'blur' (the first fix), it can lose that race on a busy A16. Also, while 'לצאת מהשלב?' or a Sheet is open, the app's window has already lost focus, so no new 'blur' comes when the user then presses Recents or Home, and the Recents card showed the board under the dialog. No JS-only approach covers that case.
items.fix: Deterministic route, as the reviewer and the bug text suggest. A new local Expo module, apps/mobile/modules/app-window (AppWindowModule.kt, same scaffold as modules/app-locale, autolinked from modules/), exposes setRecentsScreenshotEnabled(enabled) and isRecentsScreenshotToggleSupported(). It calls Activity.setRecentsScreenshotEnabled on the UI thread, guarded for API 33+ with a @RequiresApi helper. This is not FLAG_SECURE, so the player's own screenshots still work. JS wrapper src/services/recentsPicture.ts: counted holds, never throws, a no-op on iOS, below Android 13, in Jest, or on a binary without the module. levelSession takes a hold for as long as a stage session is open (taken at the end of the constructor, released in close()) when LEVEL_UI.backgroundPause is on. While it holds, Recents shows the app's plain card whatever is on top, including 'לצאת מהשלב?'. Only when the hold cannot hide (hidden: false) does the session fall back to the first round's freeze on the window's 'blur'/'focus', with the modalWindows exclusion. So on Android 13+ (the A16 runs 14) the notification shade or Samsung's screenshot bar no longer freezes the stage; that answers the review's low note about freezes beyond D65. The 'background' freeze and its 3, 2, 1 are unchanged. Spec §5.3.8 now has one line about this, marked as awaiting Moshe's approval.

items.rootCause: GameScreen (and also TapLevelScreen and PuzzleLevelScreen) took the board room's height only from onLayout. In the first render roomHeight was null, so boardSide fell back to min(width - gutters, 358 dp) and the board and keypad drew at full width. When onLayout arrived (async, about 0.5 s on the A16), they shrank to the room's height and moved.
items.fix: Unchanged from the first round; the review raised no issue here. The hook src/screens/game/useRoomHeight.ts gives the room View a callback ref that reads its laid-out height at commit through geometry.layoutHeightOf(node), using the RN element API getBoundingClientRect. In the New Architecture the tree is laid out before refs and layout effects run, so the first frame already has the final size. onLayout keeps updating the height as before, and is the only source where the API is missing (tests). Wired into GameScreen, TapLevelScreen and PuzzleLevelScreen; it changes only the source of roomHeight.

What this round fixed from the review:

It is not FLAG_SECURE, so screenshots keep working. The blur freeze stays only as a fallback where the switch does not exist (Android below 13, or an old binary).

I could not compile the Kotlin here (no APK build allowed). It copies the scaffold of modules/app-locale exactly (same gradle plugins, ModuleDefinition, return@Function, a @RequiresApi helper inside an SDK_INT check, and appContext.currentActivity, which exists in expo-modules-core's AppContext). If the gradle build fails, the error will be in AppWindowModule.kt.
  - New files are untracked: modules/app-window/, src/services/recentsPicture.ts and its test.
- Low (decisions missing from the docs): two lines added to docs/01-SPEC.md, in §5.3.8 (Recents) and §6.6 (back before the start, and back on the result), each marked 'לאישור משה'. They need Moshe's approval. On Android 13+ the shade or screenshot toolbar no longer freezes the stage, so the D65 divergence remains only in the fallback.
- Low (the result phase depended on the navigator's pop): back on the result now goes through onMap() and dismissTo, called once. Every exit from levels/play now goes through dismissTo. The root cause of why the route survived the default pop on the phone is still unexplained (it does not reproduce in Jest). The fix no longer depends on it, and the watchdog reports if dismissTo stalls.
